title: Rough Puff Pastry
description: A smart compromise between traditional puff pastry and store-bought. Quick to make with excellent rise and flakiness — the perfect everyday laminated dough. Keep everything cold and don't overwork it.

ingredients.notes: very cold, cut into 1–1.5 cm cubes

youWillNeed.note: For lifting and turning sticky dough

method.instruction: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add cold butter cubes and lightly rub them into the flour, leaving visible pea-sized pieces. Do not overwork – the chunks of butter create the flaky layers.
Add ice-cold water and mix with a fork until a rough, shaggy dough forms. The dough should be just combined, not smooth.
Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Pat into a rough rectangle, then roll into a 1 cm thick rectangle (about 20 × 40 cm).
Fold the dough into thirds like a letter. Wrap in plastic and chill for 20 minutes.
Repeat the rolling and folding process for a total of 3–4 turns, chilling 20 minutes between each turn. Rotate the dough 90° before each roll to keep it even.
After the final turn, wrap tightly and chill for at least 30 minutes before using, or up to 2 days.
For longer storage, wrap well and freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before using.

notes.title: Temperature is Everything
notes.content: Keep everything COLD. If butter softens at any point, stop and chill before continuing. Warm butter melts into the dough instead of creating layers.

notes.title: Don't Overwork
notes.content: The visible butter chunks are what create flakiness – don't blend them in completely. A shaggy, rough dough is exactly what you want. Minimal handling = better layers.

notes.title: Use Immediately or Freeze
notes.content: Use dough after the final chill for best rise. It will keep for 2 days in the fridge, but fresh is best. Freezes beautifully for up to 3 months.

notes.title: Extra Flaky
notes.content: For even more dramatic rise, do 4 full turns instead of 3. The additional lamination creates more layers without significantly increasing difficulty.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen dough overnight in the refrigerator before using.
